doc.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First trip to New York and Sheila Jordan's Hamtramck story
summary: He went to New York around 1952 with Doug Watkins, and tells how Sheila Jordan nearly got him beaten up in a Hamtramck bar.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So to put this in perspective a little bit, are we talking now the 1950’s, and you’d be in your twenties?
Well right now – no you’re getting into the ‘50’s. I went to New York the first time, maybe 1952.

See, I left out a whole lot of people, though. I left out Sheila Jordan, you know. I left out Skeeter, you know these are people who are all important to me. And when I went to New York for the first time – me and Doug went together, we stayed with Sheila Jordan, you know. Um, ‘cause Sheila Jordan is from Detroit. Her famous story is she almost got me killed.

Yeah [laughs] she come walking in that bar in Hamtramck. See I was working in a bar in Hamtramck, in Polish town. And she and this other girl came walking in there, and walked straight to us black musicians, my brother. Every eye in that joint was looking at us. Yeah, I think everybody in that joint was after us. So when the gig was over – good thing there was a streetcar going by, ‘cause we made it to that streetcar, but they was coming after us. We made it to the streetcar and got on the streetcar.
